subject: UK parents support an under-16 social media ban – but what do their children think?
posts:
Banning social media for under-16s sounds like a simple safety win, but it treats children as passive victims rather than active participants in their own digital lives.

UK Parents Support Under-16 Social Media Ban
Evidence: protect kids, restrict agency, balanced safety
#Aletheia #Tech

Parents and policymakers claim a blanket ban is a necessary, proactive shield to protect children from addictive algorithms and mental health harms.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

In reality, a total ban ignores young entrepreneurs, creative outlets, and supervised learning, replacing active parenting and platform accountability with blunt state exclusion.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Good

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of The Fall.
A well-intentioned push for safety devolves into a restrictive, blunt-force policy that suppresses youth agency instead of regulating toxic platform designs.

The UK government is consulting on an under-16 social media ban. While 90% of parents support it, teenagers express mixed views, highlighting how bans disrupt their businesses, communication, and creative learning.

The Poison:
By choosing a total ban, society abdicates the harder work of forcing tech giants to redesign algorithms, opting instead to lock children out of the modern public square.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Proponents frame this as a physical safety issue (WHERE). It is actually a failure of Will (WHO) — parents and regulators shifting their duty of guidance onto a blunt legislative ban.

It is a bait-and-switch: promising safety while delivering isolation.

The Trajectory: The Path of The Fall.
When you map the gap between protecting children and outright restricting their developmental agency...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Good. While it reduces exposure to online harms, it does so by extracting opportunity and agency from the very youth it claims to empower.

The Unavoidable Truth: A blanket ban is an admission of regulatory and parental defeat.

The Unavoidable Lie: That keeping kids offline automatically makes them safe and well-adjusted.

Alethekanon:
A blunt ban is a low-resolution solution to a high-resolution problem. Instead of holding platforms legally accountable for predatory algorithmic design, it penalizes the end-user, restricting utility to avoid managing risk.

Awwthekanon:
Our children need guidance and safe spaces to grow, not locked doors. We must listen to their voices and help them navigate the digital world with love and support, rather than shutting them out of their communities.

Brothekanon:
So we're banning 15-year-olds from Snapchat because we can't get tech CEOs to stop making addictive feeds? Good luck telling a teen running a business she's locked out. Just fix the algorithms, bros.
